english.title: Intimidate a witness / juror

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Criimal Justice and Public Order Act 1994

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing or believing that a victim, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) was

(A)_[assisting in the investigation of]_
(B)_[a witness in proceedings for]_
(C)_[a potential witness in proceedings for]_
(D)_[a juror in proceedings for]_
(E)_[a potential juror in proceedings for]_

an offence, did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY ACT..), which intimidated, and was intended to intimidate, **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), intending thereby

(F)_[to cause the investigation]_
(G)_[to cause the course of justice]_

to be obstructed, perverted or interfered with
english.legislation: Contrary to section 51(1) and (6) of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing / believing a person was
assisting investigation of offence OR
a witness / potential witness / juror / potential juror
in proceedings for offence
did an act which intimidated that person and was intended to intimidate that person
intending to cause investigation / course of justice
to be obstructed / perverted / interfered with

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The intention required for the commission of the offence need not be the only or the predominating intention with which the act is done.
(ii) The act may be done to a third party with intent to intimidate the person refereed to in the **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) field.
(iii) If the act consists of threats, the harm threatened may be financial as well as physical (whether to the person or property).
(iv) See also offence wordings: H1809 and H2235 for harming/threatening a witness/juror.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
